brief: Goldman's TMT morning note describes a global, AI-centered risk-off session: Asian and European tech equities sold off sharply, US futures fell, and AI bellwethers including NVDA, SMH and DRAM extended declines, with NVDA now lower in 9 of its last 10 sessions since the Jensen news broke. The desk ties this to a 3.3% intraday S&P reversal the prior day, poor breadth, and hawkish Fed commentary from Goolsbee and Barr that kept rate-hike odds fully priced in, with Waller and Cook scheduled to speak later that day. Company-specific drivers: Apple is reportedly building its own AI agent following Meta's Muse breakout; Intuit cut FY Consumer guidance on agentic-AI risk and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68bn, sending the stock sharply lower; Elastic fell despite Cloud acceleration because its second-half outlook was unchanged; and BILL agreed to a $6.0bn all-cash take-private by TPG and Corpay. Separately, Goldman stayed positive on China semis, Keysight beat with record orders, Globant narrowed its outlook on Middle East demand weakness, a bus tour covered ANET/CSCO/SMCI, and HSBC upgraded TSLA to Hold.
